name: get_engine_info
description: Returns the engine's version, platform, launch settings and package status. Call it first, to check that the engine is new enough and to see which toolchain packages are installed. It is fast and local: it never uses the network. Missing packages are installed automatically by the tools that need them, unless auto_install is off.

inputSchema.description: The get_engine_info tool takes no inputs.
inputSchema.title: GetEngineInfoInput

The folder with the package's programs, as an absolute path, when
the package is installed. For hosts that run one of its programs
directly, such as Verible's language server verible-verilog-ls from
the verible package. Omitted when the package isn't installed.

name.description: The package name, such as oss-cad-suite.

version.description: The package release, as a date tag (yyyy-mm-dd).

oneOf.description: Installed and intact.
Not installed.

Installed but incomplete or damaged. It is repaired when a tool needs
it, unless auto-install is off.

outputSchema.description: The engine's version, platform, launch settings and package status.

Whether the engine installs and repairs packages automatically when a
tool needs them. On by default. The host turns it off with the
--no-auto-install command-line argument.

command_line.description: The command-line arguments the engine was launched with, as given.

The engine folder, as the host set it with the --engine-folder

name: install_packages
description: Installs or repairs the engine's toolchain packages, downloading them from the internet. Packages that are already installed and intact are left alone, unless force is set to download and install them again. Other tools install the packages they need on their own, so call this only to install ahead of time, such as before going offline, or when a tool returns a setup error with the install_packages action (for example when the engine was launched with automatic install turned off). A download can take a few minutes; the tool reports progress and can be cancelled.

inputSchema.description: Which packages to install or repair.

force.description:
Download and install the packages again even if they are installed,
replacing the installed copies. Use it when a package's tools fail in
ways that suggest damaged files. Defaults to false. Don't use it while
other operations are running.

packages.description:
Names of the packages to install or repair, as get_engine_info lists
them, such as oss-cad-suite. Omitted means every package in the
engine's manifest.

name: get_catalog
description: Returns board and FPGA definitions from the engine's read-only catalog. Use it to find a board's catalog ID, such as alhambra-ii, to pass as the board of other tools, or to see a board's FPGA and how it is programmed. Each section is returned only when asked for: {"boards": {"fetch": true}} returns all boards, and {"boards": {"fetch": true, "ids": ["alhambra-ii"]}} only the listed ones. Boards include those of the request's custom_boards_file, marked custom, a custom board replacing the catalog board with its ID. The architectures section gives each FPGA family's name for people and the extension of its pin constraint files. Board descriptions are the boards' names for people.

CatalogQuery.description: Selects entries from one catalog section.

fetch.description: Whether to return this section. Defaults to false.

ids.description:
Catalog IDs of the entries to return. Omitted means all entries. An
ID that isn't in the section is an error.

DisplayPath.description: One file or folder and how to name it.

as.description:
How people read it: any text. For a folder, a path inside it keeps
its part below the folder after this and "/", or alone when this is
empty, so "" gives names relative to the folder.

path.description: The file or folder, as an absolute path.

DisplayPaths.description:
How to name paths in what people read: diagnostics, messages, testbench
output, live tool output and diagram labels. Never command lines or
fields that are paths.

files.description:
Files named as a whole. They come before folders; the first that
matches wins.

folders.description:
Folders whose files keep their path below the folder, under the
folder's name `as`. The first that matches wins.

architectures.description:
Which FPGA architectures (families) to return, by ID, such as ice40.
Omitted means none.

boards.description: Which boards to return. Omitted means none.

custom_boards_file.description:
The host's own boards: the absolute path of a JSON file that maps
board IDs to definitions in the catalog's format. board can name one
of them; one with a catalog board's ID replaces that board in this
request. Problems in the file come back as a request error with a
diagnostic for each, at line and column. Send the same file to every
tool. Omitted means none.

How to name paths in what people read (diagnostics, messages,

a whole, then folders whose files keep their path below the folder
under the folder's new name ("" gives names relative to it); the
first match in each list wins. Paths are compared by real location.
Never applied to command lines or fields that are paths. Omitted
means paths read as the request gave them.

name: lint
description: Checks Verilog and SystemVerilog sources for errors and likely mistakes with Verilator, without building. It is much faster than build and finds problems synthesis accepts, such as width mismatches. List the design files and, optionally, the testbenches; the engine doesn't search for them. The board selects the FPGA's primitive models, so designs that use them lint cleanly. Problems found are the result, not an error: passed is false and diagnostics lists each problem at file and line, with Verilator's warning code at the end of the text, which a /* verilator lint_off CODE */ comment can silence. The first call may install the toolchain package first, which takes a few minutes. Writes nothing.

name: test
description: Runs testbenches with Icarus Verilog: compiles the design files with each testbench, runs it, and reports whether it passed. A testbench fails by calling $fatal or $error, or by printing a failure line from common testbench assertion macros (*** ASSERTION FAILED or ERROR at file:line); it must end with $finish, and must not call $dumpfile, since the engine sets where its waveform goes (call $dumpvars to write one). Every listed testbench runs, even after one fails; each stops at its first failure unless stop_at_first_failure is false. A failing testbench is the result, not an error: passed is false, and each testbench's diagnostics and output say why. Compile errors are a design error with diagnostics at file and line. The first call may install the toolchain package first, which takes a few minutes. To look at a testbench's signals in a waveform viewer, use simulate.

name: simulate
description: Simulates one testbench with Icarus Verilog and opens its waveform in GTKWave: compiles the design files with the testbench, runs it to write the waveform (.vcd) into the build folder, then starts GTKWave detached and returns without waiting for it. The testbench must call $dumpvars and $finish, and must not call $dumpfile. GTKWave opens the layout file (.gtkw), which holds the signals shown; when it is missing, or is still a default one, the engine writes a default with the testbench's top-level signals, deleted again when GTKWave exits unless the user saved it; a layout the user saved is kept. Set open_viewer to false to only write the waveform, such as when no one is at the screen. A failing testbench runs to the end and is shown, with passed false and GTKWave's marker at the first failure in a default layout. Compile errors are a design error with diagnostics at file and line. To just check whether testbenches pass, use test.

A build with no changes since the last one returns at once with up_to_date set. The first build may install the toolchain package first, which takes a few minutes. name: program_board
description: Programs the bitstream of a successful build into the board it was built for. It doesn't build: call build first, and program_board only if the build succeeded. The board comes from the build, so it takes the build folder and the device to program: the id of a device from list_devices whose boards include the build's board (ask the user when several do). On ECP5, Gowin and Xilinx boards it first reads the connected FPGA's ID code and refuses a different FPGA, such as a board of another size than the build's, before writing anything. Most boards are programmed to flash, so the design stays after power-off.

DisplayPath.description: One file or folder and how to name it.

as.description:
How people read it: any text. For a folder, a path inside it keeps
its part below the folder after this and "/", or alone when this is
empty, so "" gives names relative to the folder.

path.description: The file or folder, as an absolute path.

DisplayPaths.description:
How to name paths in what people read: diagnostics, messages, testbench
output, live tool output and diagram labels. Never command lines or
fields that are paths.

files.description:
Files named as a whole. They come before folders; the first that
matches wins.

folders.description:
Folders whose files keep their path below the folder, under the
folder's name `as`. The first that matches wins.

inputSchema.description: Which build to program, and into which device.

build_folder.description: The build folder of a successful build, as an absolute path.

custom_boards_file.description:
The host's own boards: the absolute path of a JSON file that maps
board IDs to definitions in the catalog's format. board can name one
of them; one with a catalog board's ID replaces that board in this
request. Problems in the file come back as a request error with a
diagnostic for each, at line and column. Send the same file to every
tool. Omitted means none.

device.description:
The device to program: the id of a device from list_devices, such as
one whose boards include the build's board. It must still be
connected and match the board's USB filter.

display_paths.description:
How to name paths in what people read (diagnostics, messages,
testbench output, live tool output, diagram labels): files named as
a whole, then folders whose files keep their path below the folder
under the folder's new name ("" gives names relative to it); the
first match in each list wins. Paths are compared by real location.
Never applied to command lines or fields that are paths. Omitted
means paths read as the request gave them.

programmer_command.description:
A custom programmer command that replaces the board's default one,
for a custom setup. Its first word is a program from the
toolchain package, such as openFPGALoader, or an absolute path. It may
use ${VID}, ${PID}, ${BUS}, ${DEV}, ${SERIAL_NUM}, ${USB_PATH} and must use
${BITSTREAM}.

verbose.description:
Let the programmer print more detail, shown in the live output and
the logs. Not applied to a programmer_command. Defaults to false.

inputSchema.title: ProgramBoardInput

BoardMatch.description: A board a device may be.

board.description:
The board's ID: a catalog ID, or a custom board's ID when custom is
true.

custom.description:
True when the board is from the request's custom boards file rather
than the catalog's.

variants.description:
The board's variants this device fits, in the board's order, each
with its own match level. Use the level of the variant you mean,
such as the build's.

CommandRecord.description: One program the engine ran, with what it takes to run it again.

args.description:
The program as an absolute path, then its arguments, exactly as
passed.

cwd.description: The folder it ran in, as an absolute path.

package.description:
The package the program came from, with its version, such as
"oss-cad-suite 2026-10-22". Omitted for a program from elsewhere, such
as a custom programmer command.

shell.description:
One shell command line that runs it again the same way: in the same
folder, with the same minimal environment (PATH, HOME and TMPDIR).

tool.description: The program's name, such as yosys.

Device.description: A connected device that the engine can open.

boards.description:
The boards whose USB filters this device matches, best first. Empty
for a device that is no known board.

build_match.description:
How well the device matches the given build's board in the build's
variant: strong, possible or weak, as in boards. Present only when
list_devices was given a build_folder.

device.description:
USB device number on its bus. It changes when the device is plugged
in again.

id.description:
The device's ID, to pass to program_board. Opaque: don't parse it.
It names the device on this computer for a short time: it stays
valid while the device stays on the same USB port, so list the
devices again before asking the user to choose.

manufacturer.description: The manufacturer name the device reports, when available.

pid.description: USB product ID, four lowercase hex digits.

product.description: The product name the device reports, when available.

serial_number.description: The serial number the device reports, when available.

vid.description: USB vendor ID, four lowercase hex digits.

oneOf.description: A USB device.

MatchLevel.description:
How well a device matches a board, by what it means for the user, not
by its cause. The criteria are internal to the engine and change
without notice, so hosts must not infer why a device matched; they may
only show the level and compare levels (weak < possible < strong). No
level proves which board is connected.

oneOf.description: The device fits the board, but so do many other boards.

The device could be the board, but a few other boards look the
same.
The device is very likely the board.

Selector.description:
Which of a board's variants: a value of each standard dimension. In a
board definition it says where the variant sits; in requests
(board_variant) it picks the variant with these values.

connection.description:
How the computer reaches the board: usb, bootloader, ft2232h,
ft232h, cmsis-dap, usb-blaster or unspecified (see the dimensions).

memory.description:
Where the design goes: flash (kept at power-off) or ram (lost at
power-off).

VariantMatch.description: A variant of a board that a device fits.

match.description:
How well the device matches the board in this variant: strong,
possible or weak. See MatchLevel.

selector.description:
The variant's selector, such as {"connection": "usb", "memory":
"flash"}, as board_variant gives it in requests.

commands.description:
The programs this call ran, in order, each with the exact command and
a shell line that runs it again without the engine, such as for a bug
report to the tool's developers.

programmer.description:
The programmer that was used, such as openfpgaloader, or custom for a
programmer_command.
